skill.name: fp-ts-pragmatic
skill.description: Practical guidance for using fp-ts in TypeScript without heavy theory. It focuses on readable patterns for pipe, Option, Either, map, flatMap, and TaskEither.
skill.summary: Use pragmatic fp-ts patterns to write clearer TypeScript for nullable values, errors, and async workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

static_findings.snippet: Stop writing `if (x !== null && x !== undefined)` everywhere.
- `O.flatMap(fn)` = "if we have something, apply this function"
- `O.getOrElse(() => default)` = "unwrap, or use this default if nothing"
**Plain language:** `flatMap` means "if this succeeded, try the next thing"
| Default for missing | "Use this if nothing" | `O.getOrElse(() => default)` |
| Transform if present | "If something, change it" | `O.map(fn)` |
| Chain nullable operations | "If something, try this" | `O.flatMap(fn)` |
| Wrap throwing function | "Try this, catch errors" | `E.tryCatch(fn, onError)` |
| Handle both cases | "Do this for error, that for success" | `E.fold(onLeft, onRight)` |

content.value_statement: fp-ts can feel abstract when teams need practical TypeScript guidance. This skill explains the useful patterns with readable examples and clear tradeoffs.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use pipe, Option, Either, map, flatMap, and TaskEither.
Shows before-and-after refactors from imperative TypeScript to fp-ts patterns.
Gives plain-language translations for common fp-ts functions.
Helps decide when functional programming would reduce readability.
Provides quick-win patterns for nullable values, validation, and typed errors.
limitations: It is a written guide, not an automated refactoring tool.
It does not verify code against a live TypeScript project.
It focuses on common fp-ts usage, not advanced category theory.
It cannot replace team style decisions or project-specific performance testing.

use_cases.title: Refactor Null Handling
use_cases.description: Convert repeated null checks into readable Option pipelines when the result is clearer for the team.

use_cases.title: Make Errors Explicit
use_cases.description: Replace expected exceptions with Either or TaskEither results that callers must handle.

use_cases.title: Review fp-ts Readability
use_cases.description: Check whether a functional rewrite improves maintainability or should stay as simple TypeScript.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain when I should use Option, Either, and pipe in TypeScript. Keep the explanation practical and avoid theory.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this TypeScript function with pragmatic fp-ts patterns. Preserve readability and explain when plain TypeScript would be better.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Handling
prompt_templates.scenario: Choosing Either or TaskEither for a workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an fp-ts error-handling approach for this workflow. Use typed errors and show where TaskEither is useful.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Functional Complexity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this fp-ts-heavy code for unnecessary abstraction. Recommend simpler TypeScript where it would improve clarity.

output_examples.input: A function returns undefined when a user is missing.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Option when callers must handle absence, and optional chaining when the lookup is simple.

output_examples.input: A parser throws expected validation errors.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests returning Either with clear error values, then handling success and failure at the boundary.

output_examples.input: A team used pipe for every expression.
output_examples.output: The skill advises keeping pipe for multi-step transformations and using direct calls for one or two simple operations.

best_practices: Use fp-ts only when it makes the TypeScript easier to understand.
Prefer typed error values for expected failures.
Keep examples close to the team patterns already used in the codebase.
anti_patterns: Do not replace simple optional chaining with a long pipeline.
Do not introduce advanced abstractions before the team understands the basics.
Do not use fp-ts in hot paths without measuring performance.

faq.question: Does this skill teach all of fp-ts?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on the common patterns that solve most everyday TypeScript problems.

faq.question: Is this skill useful for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains fp-ts concepts in plain language and starts with practical examples.

faq.question: Can it rewrite my code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the assistant to explain, review, and suggest refactors.

faq.question: Does it require category theory knowledge?
faq.answer: No. The skill avoids theory unless it directly helps practical TypeScript work.

faq.question: When should I avoid fp-ts?
faq.answer: Avoid it when optional chaining, normal loops, or direct TypeScript code would be clearer.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
